description: Counterexamples to the tetrahedron-count heuristic for trace-field degree, correcting the guard printed in the 2026-08-11 5_2 trace-field audit. Whitehead (4 tet) and Borromean (8 tet) both have degree-2 trace field Q(i). The audit's tower-law clause is unaffected and the 5_2 result stands.

data.count_vs_degree: 4_1 figure-eight: 2 tet, deg 2; 5_2: 3 tet, deg 3; Whitehead link: 4 tet, deg 2; Borromean rings: 8 tet, deg 2
data.verdict: The guard's FIRST clause is FALSE and is corrected at source: the trace field of an n-tetrahedron hyperbolic knot is NOT generically degree n. Whitehead (4 tetrahedra = 1 regular ideal octahedron) and Borromean (8 = 2 octahedra) both have trace field Q(i), degree 2. The heuristic held for exactly the two knots the audit was looking at, 4_1 and 5_2 -- a coincidence promoted to a rule, which is the same failure mode that audit was written to correct. The SECOND clause, the tower law, is rigorous and unchanged, so the 5_2 result (Q(sqrt-7) cannot embed in a cubic) STANDS. Usable rule: do not infer the degree, COMPUTE the shape field -- solve the gluing equations, recover a shape's minimal polynomial, take its degree.

q0AnchorReason: Hyperbolic volumes (Lobachevsky/Catalan) and one exact quadratic minimal polynomial. No substrate modulus enters; the import cone reaches no q_parameter, no qou_substrate.constants, no y_lambda_at.
